sentences.text: Also in the case of electrocution, there must be points of entrance and exit of current.

9. When the current passes through body, usually symptoms like tingling, painful shock, mild or severe muscular contraction may occur which may throw the person to the ground on his face or on his back causing severe injury to the head and even dislocation of joints.
The severity of an electrical injury is directly proportional to the duration of current flow.
Typical burns are usually found at the points of entrance and exit of electrical current as at these points, skin offers resistance.
Coagulation of muscle proteins may be caused by heat and sudden liberation of steam which may also produce little cavities in the epidermis.
Skin may be split or show small greyish sharply demarcated round or oval areas and loss of epidermis at some places or blisters.
However, in the case of Late Sh. Satish Kumar, none of these symptoms were present on the body as per the postmortem report.
